title: Private Network first-run microflow and compact walkthrough screens
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact, step-focused set of first-run screens for Private/VPC onboarding that work inside the console and in a small modal for Dedicated/Appliance flows. This ticket covers: 1) a lightweight microflow diagram explaining network components and expected user inputs, 2) a 4-step compact install wizard (prep, config, validate, finish) with progressive disclosure, 3) an inline upgrade CTA and rollback safety modal, and 4) fully annotated assets for engineering handoff and localization. The visual treatment should prioritize clarity at small sizes, emphasize network safety checks, and include accessible color contrasts and screen-reader copy for each step.
acceptance_criteria: Microflow SVG and PNG exported at 1x/2x with labeled components (Edge, Control Plane, Customer VPC, Bastion).
Compact 4-step wizard screens (desktop modal width 540px) with final confirmation and retry states mocked.
Upgrade flow mockup shows version selector, pre-upgrade checklist, and a rollback confirmation microcopy.
Annotated specs: typography, spacing, iconography, animation duration (200ms), and color tokens for dark/light modes.
Accessibility notes: keyboard focus order, ARIA labels for each form field, and alt text for diagrams supplied.
Designer-to-Eng handoff doc with links to Figma, a small HTML prototype, and a GH PR template for integration.
Signoff from PM and Engineering (comments captured below).
tasks: Sketch microflow variants (linear, radial, stacked) and run quick user test with 3 SREs.
Produce compact wizard mocks (empty state, loading/validation, success, error).
Design upgrade/rollback modal and describe failure modes for engineering.
Export asset set and write handoff notes with localization keys.
Prepare a lightweight prototype demonstrating keyboard navigation and focus states.

notes_for_engineering: Microflow should be provided as an inline SVG with individual component IDs for later DOM highlighting.
Wizard step validation should be driven by a single endpoint (POST /v1/private/validate) that returns a typed error map; design shows field-level errors.
Animations: use reduced-motion preference to collapse animations and show immediate state changes.
Upgrade flow: provide a dry-run endpoint before actual upgrade; UI must show potential incompatibilities flagged by server.
Localization: text keys must be externalized; strings documented in handoff file.
Fallbacks: offline appliance flow should display a local-only troubleshooting card (mock included).
